path_to_entry: class_10: Class 10 pass with Science and Maths -> training: ITI Refrigeration & Air Conditioning trade, 1-2 years -> certification: All India Trade Test (AITT) for the National Trade Certificate under NCVT -> apprenticeship: 1-2 year apprenticeship under a licensed tradesperson or employer
entry_window: route limit: ITI admission is capped at age 40 | bypass: Employer-run apprenticeships and NSDC short-term courses have no age cap; Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) certification for existing informal workers

one_liner: Diagnoses and repairs cars, bikes and commercial vehicles.
job_roles: Auto Mechanic | Two-Wheeler Technician | Diesel Mechanic | Auto Electrician | EV Service Technician | Vehicle Body Repair Technician
entrance_exams: none
self_emp_route: Shop-floor experience, then your own garage. An established garage nets 50,000 to 1,50,000 rupees a month depending on size and whether it specialises.
ai_reason: Diagnostic computers already assist and will do more, but removing and replacing a gearbox stays physical. EV servicing is an entirely new skill demand rather than a threat. Raised clarity 20->25. A customer describes a symptom, not a fault. Working out what is actually wrong from an imprecise account is diagnostic clarity, not lookup.
path_to_entry: class_10: Class 10 pass with Science and Maths -> training: ITI Mechanic Motor Vehicle trade, 2 years -> certification: All India Trade Test (AITT) for the National Trade Certificate under NCVT -> apprenticeship: 1-2 year apprenticeship under a licensed tradesperson or employer
entry_window: route limit: ITI admission is capped at age 40 | bypass: Employer-run apprenticeships and NSDC short-term courses have no age cap; Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) certification for existing informal workers
nuances: [economics] mid_career EXCLUDES business ownership by design. Tradespeople who build a contracting firm earn far more, but the earning attribute there is entrepreneurship — Sector 5 — not the trade itself. This is why the profession does not pass the compensation filter.

one_liner: Operates excavators, cranes and earthmoving machines on sites and mines.
job_roles: Excavator Operator | Crane Operator | Bulldozer Operator | Forklift Operator | Drilling Rig Operator | Road Roller Operator
entrance_exams: none
self_emp_route: Operator, then owning a machine and hiring it out with yourself driving. The economics turn on the EMI against utilisation days, and no reliable Indian figure was found.
ai_reason: Autonomous heavy equipment exists in large open-pit mines abroad, but Indian sites are congested, unstructured and cost-sensitive. Operator demand tracks infrastructure spending, which is rising.
path_to_entry: class_10: Class 8 pass is enough for this trade -> training: ITI Heavy Equipment Operation trade, 6 months to 1 year -> certification: All India Trade Test (AITT) for the National Trade Certificate under NCVT -> apprenticeship: 1-2 year apprenticeship under a licensed tradesperson or employer
entry_window: route limit: ITI admission is capped at age 40 | bypass: Employer-run apprenticeships and NSDC short-term courses have no age cap; Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) certification for existing informal workers
review_reason: SELF-EMPLOYMENT CEILING OWED. Employed mid-career is 5.5 lakh and people in this profession routinely go independent, but no reliable Indian figure was found for what they earn once they do. Until it exists the record understates the profession, which is exactly the defect this field was added to fix. The route is recorded; the number is not.

one_liner: Measures land and sites precisely so that construction can be planned.
job_roles: Land Surveyor | Total Station Operator | Drone Survey Technician | Cadastral Surveyor | Setting-out Engineer
entrance_exams: none
self_emp_route: Survey experience, then your own practice with a total station and drone, billing per project for plot demarcation, layout and DGPS work.
ai_reason: Drone and automated processing take over the calculation and mapping, but someone must still stand on the land, set control points and resolve what the boundary actually is. More exposed than the other trades, still low.
path_to_entry: class_10: Class 10 pass with Science and Maths -> training: ITI Surveyor trade, 1-2 years -> certification: All India Trade Test (AITT) for the National Trade Certificate under NCVT -> apprenticeship: 1-2 year apprenticeship under a licensed tradesperson or employer
entry_window: route limit: ITI admission is capped at age 40 | bypass: Employer-run apprenticeships and NSDC short-term courses have no age cap; Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) certification for existing informal workers
review_reason: SELF-EMPLOYMENT CEILING OWED. Employed mid-career is 5.25 lakh and people in this profession routinely go independent, but no reliable Indian figure was found for what they earn once they do. Until it exists the record understates the profession, which is exactly the defect this field was added to fix. The route is recorded; the number is not.

one_liner: Turns engineers' and architects' ideas into precise technical drawings.
job_roles: CAD Draughtsman (Civil) | CAD Draughtsman (Mechanical) | BIM Technician | Technical Detailer | 3D Modelling Technician
entrance_exams: none
self_emp_route: Freelance drafting for architects and small consultancies, usually per drawing.
ai_reason: THE EXCEPTION AMONG THE TRADES. Purely digital execution with low clarity — generative CAD and text-to-drawing tools hit this directly. Every other trade here is protected by physical work; this one is not. The safer path is to use it as an entry point into BIM coordination or a diploma in civil or mechanical engineering.
failed_rules: mid_career 3.75 < floor 4.5 ; mid_career 3.75 < 6.0 with ai_exposure high
path_to_entry: class_10: Class 10 pass with Science and Maths -> training: ITI Draughtsman (Civil / Mechanical) trade, 1-2 years -> certification: All India Trade Test (AITT) for the National Trade Certificate under NCVT -> apprenticeship: 1-2 year apprenticeship under a licensed tradesperson or employer
entry_window: route limit: ITI admission is capped at age 40 | bypass: Employer-run apprenticeships and NSDC short-term courses have no age cap; Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) certification for existing informal workers
review_reason: SELF-EMPLOYMENT CEILING OWED. Employed mid-career is 3.75 lakh and people in this profession routinely go independent, but no reliable Indian figure was found for what they earn once they do. Until it exists the record understates the profession, which is exactly the defect this field was added to fix. The route is recorded; the number is not.
nuances: [demand_signal] Demand is declining, not merely low. Parametric CAD, scan-to-BIM and generative tools absorb the drawing work itself, so the total number of pure draughting posts is shrinking rather than staying small. The profession is still listed because the work exists and pays today, and because it remains one of the shortest routes into a technical career without a degree - but the trend is downward and the record says so.

one_liner: Runs the machines and chemistry that turn fibre into fabric.
job_roles: Textile Technologist | Spinning Technologist | Weaving Technologist | Dyeing & Finishing Chemist | Technical Textiles Engineer | Textile Quality Executive
entrance_exams: JEE Main Paper 1 | JEE Advanced | BITSAT | VITEEE | SRMJEEE | COMEDK
self_emp_route: Own processing or job-work unit, or sourcing consultancy for buyers.
ai_reason: Mill work is physical and process-bound — spinning, weaving and dyeing happen on machines, not screens. Production planning is partly exposed; diagnosing why a batch dyed unevenly is not.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Maths compulsory, plus one of Chemistry/Biology/Vocational -> entrance_exam: JEE Main Paper 1, or a state or private engineering entrance -> degree: B.Tech in Textile Technology / Textile Engineering (4 years) -> specialisation: Internships and plant or site exposure decide who gets hired
entry_window: route limit: JEE Main — admits only recent class 12 passouts | bypass: 3-year engineering diploma, then lateral entry into B.Tech year 2 (generally no upper age limit); B.Sc graduate lateral entry into B.Tech year 2; Private university admission
nuances: [professional_sector] Textile ENGINEERING sits here — fibre science, machinery, dyeing chemistry. Apparel and fashion PRODUCTION sits in Sector 8 as craft. The same split as Architect here versus Interior Designer in Sector 8. || [demand_signal] Do not read the size of the industry as the size of the profession. There are about 50 B.Tech textile engineering programmes in India, 20 government and 29 private, concentrated in IIT Delhi, ICT Mumbai, VJTI, NIT Jalandhar and Anna University. Core textile-engineering openings are few and a large share of graduates take non-core jobs, which is why the demand tag is low while the industry it serves is vast. Starting pay in core roles is around 4 lakh, consistent with the band shown.

one_liner: Designs and looks after the machines that hospitals use to diagnose and treat.
job_roles: Biomedical Engineer | Clinical Engineer (hospital) | Medical Device Design Engineer | Medical Imaging Systems Engineer | Regulatory Affairs Engineer (devices) | Biomedical Equipment Technician | Hospital Equipment Maintenance Technician | Medical Device Service Engineer | Calibration Technician | Equipment Installation Specialist
entrance_exams: JEE Main Paper 1 | JEE Advanced | BITSAT | VITEEE | SRMJEEE | COMEDK
ai_reason: Devices are physical and safety-critical, and hospital clinical engineering means hands on equipment people's lives depend on. Design documentation is exposed; commissioning an MRI is not.
role_spread: [Clinical Engineer (hospital)] higher: emotional_intelligence, extraversion, agreeableness / lower: spatial || [Biomedical Equipment Technician, Hospital Equipment Maintenance Technician, Medical Device Service Engineer, Calibration Technician, Equipment Installation Specialist] higher: bodily, conscientiousness, attention_span / lower: spatial, openness
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Maths compulsory, plus one of Chemistry/Biology/Vocational -> entrance_exam: JEE Main Paper 1, or a state or private engineering entrance -> degree: B.Tech in Biomedical Engineering (4 years) -> specialisation: Internships and plant or site exposure decide who gets hired
entry_window: route limit: JEE Main — admits only recent class 12 passouts | bypass: 3-year engineering diploma, then lateral entry into B.Tech year 2 (generally no upper age limit); B.Sc graduate lateral entry into B.Tech year 2; Private university admission
nuances: [degree_dependency] Tagged undergrad because that is the DESTINATION for design, regulatory and clinical engineering work. It is not a door. The service and calibration half of this profession is genuinely reachable on a two-year diploma, and a diploma holder converges on the same mid-career band - which is why Biomedical Equipment Technician is a job role here rather than a profession of its own. || [job_roles] Biomedical Equipment Technician was a separate profession until it failed the merge test: same object of concern, same industry, and the two records had written the SAME demand sentence from opposite ends, with an identical mid-career midpoint of 7 lakh. It differed only in entry route, and entry route is not a skill set. Folded in as job roles, with the split recorded in role_spread. || [licensing_body] The NCAHP Act's ninth category, Medical Technologists and Physician Associate, names Biomedical Engineer as a covered title. That Act regulates allied health PRACTICE inside Indian clinical care; it does not gate device design, manufacture or field service, so no licensing body is named here.

one_liner: Stops industrial accidents and fires before they happen, and plans what to do if they do.
job_roles: Health, Safety & Environment (HSE) Officer | Fire Protection Systems Designer | Industrial Safety Engineer | Loss Prevention Engineer | Safety Auditor | Process Safety Engineer
industrial_sectors: CSDCI | HYSSC | SMSSC | IISSSC | PSSC | CGSC
entrance_exams: JEE Main Paper 1 | JEE Advanced | BITSAT | VITEEE | SRMJEEE | COMEDK
self_emp_route: Own safety consultancy and audit practice serving factories and buildings.
ai_reason: Inspection is physical and site-based, and accountability for a preventable death cannot be delegated to software. Checklist generation and report writing are exposed; walking a plant and seeing what is about to go wrong is not.
role_spread: [Safety Auditor, Loss Prevention Engineer] higher: dogmatism, conscientiousness, verbal / lower: bodily, extraversion
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Maths compulsory, plus one of Chemistry/Biology/Vocational -> entrance_exam: JEE Main Paper 1, or a state or private engineering entrance -> degree: B.Tech in Fire & Safety / Industrial Safety Engineering (4 years) -> specialisation: Internships and plant or site exposure decide who gets hired
entry_window: route limit: JEE Main — admits only recent class 12 passouts | bypass: 3-year engineering diploma, then lateral entry into B.Tech year 2 (generally no upper age limit); B.Sc graduate lateral entry into B.Tech year 2; Private university admission
nuances: [job_roles] The statutory Safety Officer post under Section 40B of the Factories Act is NOT listed here because it is not an entry role — state rules require an engineering degree PLUS five years of experience. It is what this career grows into. Entry is HSE work in construction and oil and gas, usually with a NEBOSH certification alongside the degree. || [licensing_body] Null despite the statutory mandate. Section 40B requires factories to APPOINT a Safety Officer; it does not licence the person. There is no register and no bar on practising without it, so this is not Tier A licensing.

one_liner: Flies drones for a living — spraying crops, surveying land, inspecting bridges and towers.
job_roles: Drone Pilot | Agricultural Spraying Drone Operator | Survey Drone Operator | Infrastructure Inspection Pilot | Drone Data Processing Technician | Drone Maintenance Technician
industrial_sectors: AASSC | ASCI | CSDCI | IESC | SCGJ | EXT-DEFENCE | LSC
entrance_exams: DGCA RPTO written and practical assessment
self_emp_route: Own drone and a DGCA remote pilot certificate, billing per survey, spray or inspection job.
ai_reason: Flying is physical and site-based, and a licensed human is legally responsible for the aircraft. Flight planning and image processing are exposed; being accountable for a machine over a public road is not. Automation increases drone USE rather than removing the pilot.
path_to_entry: class_10: Class 10 pass is the only education requirement -> medical: DGCA medical certificate; minimum age 18 -> training: Training at a DGCA-approved Remote Pilot Training Organisation (RPTO) -> licence: Pass written and practical assessment for the Remote Pilot Certificate
entry_window: HARD BLOCK: Remote Pilot Certificate is issued only between ages 18 and 65
nuances: [class12_prerequisite] Class 10 pass is the only educational requirement — no class 12, no degree. This is the most accessible statutorily licensed profession in the taxonomy, and one of very few Tier A careers open to someone who left school early.

one_liner: Works in dust-free cleanrooms making chips, medicines and precision parts.
job_roles: Semiconductor Fab Technician | Cleanroom Operator (Pharma) | Wafer Process Technician | Precision Assembly Technician | Metrology Technician | Fab Equipment Maintenance Technician
entrance_exams: none
ai_reason: Cleanroom work is physical, procedural and cannot be done remotely — someone must gown up and handle wafers or vials. Process monitoring is partly automated; hands in the cleanroom are not.
path_to_entry: class_10_12: Class 10 or 12; a science background helps -> training: ITI or diploma in electronics, instrumentation or chemical plant operation -> certification: Cleanroom protocol and GMP training, usually given by the employer -> on_job: Process and equipment specialisation on the line — this is where pay rises
entry_window: route limit: ITI admission is capped at age 40 | bypass: Employer-run apprenticeships and NSDC short courses have no age cap; Recognition of Prior Learning for existing manufacturing workers
nuances: [profession] Deliberately broader than 'Semiconductor Fab Technician'. A coverage probe found no existing profession covering cleanroom process work, but naming it after semiconductors alone would bet the record on one emerging industry. Pharma cleanroom operation is the same skill set and employs large numbers in India today. || [economics] The salary band is shipped at its current level and rests in part on the India Semiconductor Mission delivering operational fabs at scale. Pharmaceutical and medical-device cleanroom demand is established and carries the record on its own; the semiconductor half is the part that depends on a policy cycle landing.

one_liner: Designs and runs nuclear reactors, and keeps the radiation safely contained.
job_roles: Reactor Design Engineer | Reactor Operations Engineer | Radiation Safety Officer | Nuclear Fuel Cycle Engineer | Nuclear Instrumentation Engineer | Radioactive Waste Management Engineer
entrance_exams: JEE Main Paper 1 | GATE | BARC OCES / DGFS | BITSAT | VITEEE
ai_reason: Among the most consequence-heavy engineering work there is — a licensed, accountable human is required at every safety decision. Simulation is exposed; deciding whether a reactor is safe to restart is not.
path_to_entry: class_11_12: Physics and Maths compulsory -> entrance_exam: JEE Main, or a state or private engineering entrance -> degree: B.Tech in Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Electronics, Metallurgy or Nuclear — or M.Sc Physics/Chemistry -> gate: Clear GATE — this is the real gate into the Department of Atomic Energy -> training: One-year BARC Training School course via OCES or DGFS, then appointment as Scientific Officer
entry_window: route limit: JEE Main — admits only recent class 12 passouts | bypass: 3-year engineering diploma, then lateral entry into B.Tech year 2; B.Sc graduate lateral entry into B.Tech year 2; M.Sc Physics or Chemistry route into OCES, which bypasses B.Tech entirely
nuances: [path_to_entry] You do NOT need a nuclear engineering degree. BARC recruits from Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Electronics, Metallurgy, Physics and Chemistry — GATE is the real gate, not the branch name. An M.Sc Physics graduate can enter OCES without any B.Tech at all. || [economics] The band is shipped as it stands and reflects central government Scientific Officer pay scales. Those carry allowances, subsidised housing and pension terms that do not appear in a CTC figure, so comparison with a private-sector offer of the same number understates the government package.
